de.my_domain.abalone.gui

Class GameFrame

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.awt.Component
      • java.awt.Container
        • java.awt.Window
          • java.awt.Frame
            • javax.swing.JFrame
              • de.my_domain.abalone.gui.GameFrame
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    java.awt.image.ImageObserver, java.awt.MenuContainer, java.io.Serializable, javax.accessibility.Accessible, javax.swing.RootPaneContainer, javax.swing.WindowConstants

    public class GameFrame
extends javax.swing.JFrame
    The GameFrame Class. The GameFrame class is a JFrame. It is used as the window of a Board board. It holds a BallPanel to display the board, as well as a ButtonPanel to enable the user to communicate with Abalone. It also hold the board logic and does the communication with the Board interface of the board. For this it offers methods such as a move, so another class can provoke a human as well as a machine move on the Board model. The GameFrame class also implements methods to send messages to the user via a pop up window, to create a new board automatically reading the values set in the drop down menus of the ButtonPanel, a method to ask if the machine is doing something and a getter method of the current Board.

    • Constructor Detail

      • GameFrame

        public GameFrame(int startingSize,
                 int startingLevel,
                 Player first)
        The GameFrame constructor creates a new JFrame window for the Abalone board. It first creates a new Abalone model, which is saved as a instance variable, then creates the BoardPanel, which represents the Board and the ButtonPanel for changing settings. The Board also has a minimum size which ensures a good representation of the content.
        Parameters:
        startingSize - The initial size of the Abalone board is given here.
        startingLevel - The initial level of the Abalone board is given here.
        first - The initial player of the Abalone board is given here.

    • Method Detail

      • customizeLayout

        private void customizeLayout()
        The customizeLayout method sets the layout of the JPanel to a BorderLayout which has the board panel in the center and the button panel, which allows the player to change settings, on the south

      • getModel

        Board getModel()
        The getModel method is a getter method for the Board object saved in GameFrame. This method can be used to ask for certain properties of the current board via the board interface.
        Returns:
        The current Board model is returned.

      • setModel

        private void setModel(Board model)
        The setModel method is an advanced setter method for the Board attribute model. It takes a Board object and sets the old model to the new. The method then initiates an repaint on the BoardPanel. The method must not be called with a board from another size, since it only does a repaint on the balls of the board and does not create a new board with more or less balls.
        Parameters:
        model - The model, to which the current model is set.

      • newGame

        void newGame(Player first)
        The newGame method creates a new board using the size and the level which are selected in the ButtonPanel. The player variable determines which Player is allowed to make the first move.
        Parameters:
        first - The player, who is allowed to make the first move.

      • award

        private void award()
        The award method should only be called if model.isGameOver() == true. It tells the human user of the program which player has won the board.

      • message

        void message(java.lang.String message)
        The message method creates a new JOptionPane to send a message to the user of the program via a popup window. The center of the popup window is set to the GameFrame.
        Parameters:
        message - The message which needs to be displayed.

      • makeMove

        void makeMove(int firstRow,
              int firstDiag,
              int row,
              int diag)
        The makeMove method takes care of the human as well as the machine move. After the human move is done it checks whether the board is over, makes a machine move or message the user when it can make another move. It also checks if the human move was not valid and then messages the user.
        Parameters:
        firstRow - The row coordinate of the Ball the human wants to move.
        firstDiag - The diag coordinate of the Ball the human wants to move.
        row - The row coordinate the human wants the selected ball to move to.
        diag - The diag coordinate the human wants the selected ball to move to.

      • makeMachineMove

        private void makeMachineMove()
        The makeMachineMove method creates a new Thread in which the machine move can run. After the machine move has stopped it calls the method updateAfterMachineMove in the EventDispatcher, which then takes care of updating the view. The method also checks if a run flag is set to true. if the run flag is set to false, the flag avoids the machine to continue running.

      • updateAfterMachineMove

        private void updateAfterMachineMove(Board nextModel)
        The updateAfterMachineMove method sets the, by the machine calculated, model to be the new model, and then checks if the board is either over of if the machine can run again. It also conducts this move. The method also checks if a run flag is set to true. if the run flag is set to false, the flag avoids the machine to continue running.
        Parameters:
        nextModel - The nextModel Board is the the new, by the machine calculated, model.

      • isMachineBusy

        private boolean isMachineBusy()
        The isMachineBusy method checks if the machine is currently running. It uses the isAlive flag of the Thread object for this. It first checks if a thread objects exists at all.
        Returns:
        true if a Thread exists and if it is running. false if either no Thread exists or if the Thread is not running.

      • stopMachineMove

        private void stopMachineMove(boolean runAgain)
        The stopMachineMove method first sets the run flag to false in order to avoid that the updateAfterMachineMove method can start another machine thread while ending the current thread. Then it ends the machine move using the deprecated method Thread.stop(). This is the only option to prematurely end the machine thread before it ends itself, since an interrupted flag could only be checked by the machine move either before the calculation has begun or at the time, when the thread would have quit anyway.
        Parameters:
        runAgain - The runAgain must be set to true if the current session needs to be continued, and to false if the program is determined to end immediately.
